verdicts.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper drops sliding_window and softcap, silently disabling Mistral/Gemma2 windowed attention and Gemma2 logit softcapping
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced both halves independently on the current tree (transformers 5.15.1, torch 2.14). Code chain verified line by line: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/qkv.py:155-164 calls attention_interface(self, q, k, v, attention_mask, dropout=..., scaling=self.scaling, **kwargs) with no sliding_window and no softcap, while upstream .venv/.../transformers/models/mistral/modeling_mistral.py:172 passes sliding_window=getattr(self.config,'sliding_window',None) and models/gemma2/modeling_gemma2.py:281-282 passes both sliding_window=self.sliding_window and softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping. The dedicated wrappers qkv_gemma3.py:83 and qkv_qwen3.py:81 do pass sliding_window, confirming the generic wrapper is the outlier. Only mistral.py, ministral.py and gemma2.py install apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch, whose vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask (runtime/masking.py:132-143) returns None on the no-padding SDPA prefill and delegates the band to vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window (components/attention.py:279-315), which only applies it when the sliding_window kwarg is not None. REPRO 1 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/v80/mistral_sw.py): 1-layer Mistral, sliding_window=4, seq_len=16, sdpa, no attention_mask, PEFT LoRA on q/k/v, apply_model_patches(..., lora=True), fused path reached by installing a reference _opaque_fused_qkv and forcing Tensor.is_cuda: 'plain SW vs opaque unfused = 0.0' (opaque's own unfused path is bit-exact with upstream) but 'plain SW vs opaque FUSED = 0.3116' on a logit scale of 0.573, and 'plain causal vs opaque FUSED = 0.0' exactly -- the fused output is bit-identical to the same weights with sliding_window=None, so the window is entirely gone. REPRO 2 (v80/gemma2_softcap.py): 1-layer Gemma2, attn_logit_softcapping=0.05, both eager and sdpa: 'base vs opaque unfused = 0.0' but 'nocap vs opaque FUSED = 0.000000' exactly while 'base(softcap) vs nocap = 6.5e-05' -- the fused output is bit-identical to the softcap-disabled model, proving softcap is never passed (the absolute magnitude is small only because the model is randomly initialized; the substitution is total). No guard makes this unreachable: _lora_patching_allowed() returns True whenever CUDA+triton are present, apply_peft_model_patches defaults lora=performance=True, sdpa is the HF default, and grep shows no test in packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/ mentions sliding_window or softcap and none exercises _make_fused_qkv_attention_forward. Secondary claim I could NOT verify for lack of CUDA/flash-attn: the same kwarg drop should also void the window for flash_attention_* on Qwen2/Cohere2, because _backend_enforces_sliding_window (masking.py:42-48) deliberately leaves the band out of the mask for flash backends; the eager/sdpa dense-mask path for those two families does materialize the band, so they are unaffected there, matching the finding's own note. Keeping severity high: it is a silent, default-on deviation from the target architecture in the advertised 'numerically equivalent' fused path, though it touches utility only (affects_epsilon false).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: CUDA host with triton, a PEFT model with LoRA on q_proj/k_proj/v_proj, and apply_model_patches(model) (lora defaults to True) so _auto_fuse_lora installs the generic fused QKV wrapper. (a) Gemma2 + LoRA loses attention-logit softcapping in every fused layer at every sequence length and in both eager and sdpa: verified bit-identical to running the same weights with attn_logit_softcapping=None. (b) Mistral / Ministral / Gemma2 lose the sliding window whenever the compact SDPA prefill path is taken -- attn_implementation='sdpa', attention_mask=None (no padding), no KV cache, attention_dropout==0, and query length > config.sliding_window (4096 for stock Mistral-7B and Gemma2): verified bit-identical to the same weights with sliding_window=None, i.e. every query attends to the whole prefix. The opaque unfused path is bit-exact with upstream in both cases, so the defect is confined to the fused wrapper. Qwen2/Cohere2 under eager/sdpa are unaffected (their dense masking patcher materializes the band); the flash-attention variant of the same drop is plausible but untested here.

verdicts.title: Fused QKV never got the fp32-adapter fallback that #977 added to the LoRA Linear and MLP paths
verdicts.reasoning: The incomplete-fix claim is exactly right, but the established magnitude is bf16-rounding level, so I am downgrading medium -> low. Verified from git: `git show --stat 5b41925c` ('fix(patches): preserve fused LoRA mixed-precision behavior (#977)') touches components/_utils.py (adds _active_adapters_use_dtype/_lora_projections_use_dtype), linear.py and mlp.py -- and NOT qkv.py. Current tree: linear.py:52-55 and mlp.py:58-62 both early-out to PEFT's own forward when `not torch.is_autocast_enabled('cuda') and not <adapters already in target dtype>`; qkv.py:55-65 has no such check and unconditionally does hidden_states.to(_active_lora_dtype(hidden_states)), after which Opaque_LoRA_QKV.forward (kernels/lora.py:512-514) calls cast_to_dtype(active_cuda_dtype(X), ...) which, with autocast off, is X.dtype -- so fp32 lora_A/lora_B are cast down to bf16. grep confirms the two helpers are referenced only from _utils.py, linear.py and mlp.py. REPRO (/tmp/.../scratchpad/v80/mixedprec.py, /tmp/.../v80/mixedprec_grad.py): 1-layer Llama .to(bfloat16), get_peft_model with LoRA on q/k/v/o (lora_A stays float32), autocast OFF, Tensor.is_cuda forced. Kernel-call tracing shows only ['Opaque_LoRA_QKV'] is invoked -- Opaque_LoRA_W correctly declines for o_proj, exactly the inconsistency claimed. Forward logits differ from the PEFT reference by 2.08e-3 on a scale of 0.512, i.e. about one bf16 ulp of the output (0.512*2^-8 = 2.00e-3). Adapter-gradient relative max error: q_proj.lora_A 4.6e-3, q_proj.lora_B 8.8e-3 (o_proj shows 3-4e-3 purely as downstream contamination from the bf16 q/k/v activations). Test gap confirmed: packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_fused_lora_qkv.py:58 and :123 both wrap their bodies in `with torch.autocast('cuda', ...)`, the branch the guard skips; nothing pins the no-autocast QKV case. So: real, structurally confirmed inconsistency with the deliberate #977 fix, but the observed error is at bf16 rounding, not a wrong result -- low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: CUDA host with triton, model.to(torch.bfloat16) then get_peft_model(...) so lora_A/lora_B stay fp32, LoRA on q/k/v (and optionally o/MLP), forward run WITHOUT torch.autocast. o_proj and the MLP take the #977 fallback and keep their fp32 adapter arithmetic; the fused Q/K/V path has no such guard and casts the fp32 adapters to bf16 inside Opaque_LoRA_QKV. Measured on a 1-layer Llama: logits differ from the PEFT reference by ~1 bf16 ulp (2.1e-3 on a 0.51 scale) and the q/k/v adapter gradients by 0.5-0.9% relative. No silent wrong result, just loss of the fp32-adapter precision that #977 deliberately preserved elsewhere, plus an untested branch (both existing QKV mixed-precision tests run under autocast).

verdicts.title: Fused QKV validates its preconditions only at patch time and reads only active_adapters[0], so adapter switching silently drops dropout and extra adapters
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves reproduced. Code chain: _router.py:70-97 evaluates _has_lora / _bias_is_frozen / _no_lora_dropout once inside _auto_fuse_lora and then installs attn.forward = types.MethodType(fused_qkv_fwd, attn) with attn._opaque_lora_qkv_patched = True; nothing re-checks. components/_utils.py:46-58 (_extract_lora_params) returns early on disable_adapters/no active adapters but otherwise uses only `active = lora_linear.active_adapters[0]`. The sibling path does both things the fused path omits: linear.py:37-47 recomputes dropout_is_noop per call and returns `original(self, x, ...)` when dropout is live, and linear.py:75-83 explicitly folds in `self.active_adapters[1:]`. REPRO (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/v80/adapters.py, 1-layer Llama, PEFT LoRA on q/k/v, apply_model_patches(..., lora=True), Tensor.is_cuda forced so the fused branch runs): (a) after m.add_adapter('noisy', LoraConfig(lora_dropout=0.9, ...)) + set_adapter('noisy') + m.train(), the module reports active ['noisy'] with Dropout(p=0.9) yet the spread across four fused forwards is exactly 0.0, while the same four forwards through the unfused PEFT path spread by 0.911 -- dropout is silently skipped on q/k/v (and the fused path does use the noisy adapter's weights, so the user gets the new adapter with none of its regularization). (b) with set_adapter(['default','b']) the module reports active ['default','b'], yet 'peft(a) vs fused(a+b) = 0.0' exactly while 'peft(a) vs peft(a+b) = 0.595' -- adapter b's q/k/v contribution is entirely absent, so its q/k/v parameters would receive no gradient. Patch-time gating itself is fine (I re-read _router.py:70-97 and the existing routing tests in test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:85-111 pin partial-target/dropout/trainable-bias skips), so the defect is strictly about post-patch adapter mutation. Keeping medium rather than high: it is a silent wrong result, but it needs non-default PEFT multi-adapter usage after patching and only bites on CUDA (the non-CUDA wrapper falls back to the unmodified forward). No epsilon impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: CUDA host with triton; a PEFT model patched by apply_model_patches(..., lora=True) whose adapter at patch time had lora_dropout=0 (the gate requirement). Afterwards the user mutates the adapter set, which the fused wrapper never re-validates: (a) add_adapter(name, LoraConfig(lora_dropout=p>0)) + set_adapter(name) + train() -> the fused Q/K/V use the new adapter's weights but apply no dropout (verified: 0.0 stochastic spread over four forwards vs 0.911 through PEFT), while o_proj and the MLP still apply it; (b) set_adapter(['a','b']) -> the fused Q/K/V apply only adapter a (verified bit-identical to the a-only PEFT output, 0.595 away from the correct a+b output), so adapter b's q/k/v parameters get no gradient, while linear.py correctly folds extra adapters into o_proj. Unpatched/non-CUDA runs and unmutated adapter sets are unaffected.

verdicts.title: Fused QKV wrapper closes over a bound original_forward, so a deepcopy of a patched model routes the copy's fallback to the original model's attention
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism is real and I reproduced it exactly, but the cited reachable call site is refuted, so I am downgrading medium -> low. Mechanism: _router.py:89-94 does attn._opaque_fused_qkv = types.MethodType(_opaque_fused_lora_qkv, attn) then fused_qkv_fwd = fused_forward_factory(attn.forward) and attn.forward = types.MethodType(fused_qkv_fwd, attn). copy.deepcopy's _deepcopy_method rebinds __self__ to the copy but treats __func__ (a plain function) as atomic, so the closure cell holding the ORIGINAL bound attn.forward is shared. REPRO (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/v80/dc.py, plain CPU, no is_cuda forcing so the fallback at qkv.py:109-117 is the live path): 'clone.forward.__self__ is clone attn: True', 'closure cells bound to ORIGINAL attn: [True]' / 'to CLONE attn: [False]', '_opaque_fused_qkv __self__ is clone attn: True' (so that method is indeed safe, as the finding says); after attn.q_proj.lora_B['default'].weight.add_(5.0) on the ORIGINAL only, the clone's logits move by 0.184 and become bit-identical to the original's (diff 0.0) -- the clone's attention is fully aliased. The identical bound-method capture exists for MLP too (_router.py:135 `_make_fused_lora_mlp_forward(mlp.forward, ...)`), while linear.py is safe because _router.py passes the unbound `type(module).forward`. REFUTED part -- the failure scenario. copy.deepcopy of a model appears exactly once in packages/*/src (`grep -rn 'copy.deepcopy'`): _dpo_trainer.py:729, inside _setup_tr_dpo. But _dpo_trainer.py:396-403 raises ConfigurationError('sync_ref_model (TR-DPO) requires full fine-tuning, not PEFT') whenever _sync_ref_model and _is_peft, and _setup_tr_dpo is only reached for sync_ref_model=True, whereas _auto_fuse_lora only installs the wrapper on PEFT LoRA modules. So the TR-DPO reference-model scenario cannot occur. Additionally, on CUDA -- the only place the fused kernels are meant to run -- hidden_states.is_cuda is True, the fallback is never taken, and the aliasing is invisible; it only bites on CPU/MPS, where _lora_patching_allowed() still installs the wrapper (torch.cuda.is_available() False -> True) and the fallback is the sole path. No epsilon impact, no in-library caller: low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: User code (not the Opaque library itself) does copy.deepcopy on a PEFT model already patched by apply_model_patches(..., lora=True) -- e.g. a hand-rolled reference/EMA/eval snapshot -- and then runs the copy on CPU or MPS. Because the generic and dedicated fused wrappers close over the original instance's bound forward and deepcopy shares that closure, every non-CUDA forward on the copy executes the ORIGINAL module's attention with the ORIGINAL weights. Verified on CPU: after mutating only the original's lora_B, the clone's logits changed by 0.184 and matched the original's exactly. The same bound capture affects the fused MLP wrapper; the LoRA Linear wrapper is unaffected because it captures type(module).forward. Not reachable through Opaque's own code: the library's only model deepcopy (_dpo_trainer.py:729, TR-DPO) is gated off for PEFT models by the ConfigurationError at _dpo_trainer.py:396-403, and on a CUDA run the aliased fallback branch is never executed.
